what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted 4-2 to recommend approval of the tax increment financing warrant article for the special town meeting.
Members split on whether the charter's public hearing requirement was met for the agreement with an agricultural company.
The chair said votes will be confirmed at special town meeting, where members can change them on the floor.
On the capital plan threshold, the committee will take no action until it hears from the capital planning committee, possibly in a joint discussion.
The town manager said remote learning equipment will be charged to CARES Act funding and some of that money may go unused.

why_it_matters: The tax increment financing agreement exempts part of a company's property tax in exchange for expected growth in the tax rolls, so it affects how much revenue the town gives up now against what it may collect later.
Residents at the special town meeting will be asked to vote on the article, and the committee's 4-2 recommendation is advice that the meeting can accept or reject.
A higher capital plan threshold would change which purchases and projects get reviewed as capital items, and that decision is still open.
watch_next: The special town meeting vote on the tax increment financing warrant article.
A possible joint discussion with the capital planning committee on the capital plan threshold.
